question: A task list had 44 items. In the morning, it tripled. By noon, 31 items were completed. By afternoon, 35 items were added. By evening, 8 more arrived. The final list was divided in half by priority. A distractor: another list had 75 items. How many items (in terms of half-size units—when converted to half-lists) were in the main list?

A delivery had 219 packages in the morning. By mid-morning, 27 more arrived. By noon, 33 were added. By afternoon, the count multiplied by 8. By late afternoon, 8 more were received. The total was divided into 5 equal routes. By evening, 48 packages were added to the final count. A distractor: another delivery had 95 packages. How many packages were delivered?

An account had 169 dollars initially. In the morning, 43 dollars were added. By noon, the total multiplied by 5. By afternoon, it was divided by 5 (undoing the multiplication). Then 191 dollars were spent. By evening, 19 more was removed. A distractor: his brother had 85 dollars in a separate account. How much was left (comparing both accounts in the narrative)?

A company had 90 employees in the morning. By mid-morning, the count quadrupled. By late morning, 70 more were hired. By afternoon, this doubled. By evening, everything doubled again. Their rival company had 150 employees (separate count). How many total employees did the company have by end of day?

A warehouse started with 238 items. In the morning, 63 items arrived. By midday, 176 were shipped out. The remaining were divided equally into 5 storage areas. Then 23 more items came in. Another 27 were added. The count tripled. A distractor: another warehouse had 95 items. How many items were in the final count (measured in triple batches)?

A production line had 140 units. It multiplied by 7 (shift boost). Then by 7 more (efficiency gain). The count was divided by 5 (split into groups). By midday, 401 units were removed. By afternoon, 769 more units were lost. By evening, 24 units arrived. When converted to dozens (unit change), how many dozen units remained?

A workforce had 161 employees initially. It multiplied by 9 (shift expansion). Then 74 more were hired. By afternoon, the count multiplied by 5. By evening, it multiplied by 5 again. His colleague managed 95 employees (separate count). How many employees did the company end up with (measured in 5-person teams)?

A budget started at 147 dollars. In the morning, 58 dollars were spent. By noon, 16 dollars were refunded. By afternoon, 10 more arrived. Then 114 dollars were withdrawn. By evening, the remaining tripled and was converted to fifty-cent units (unit change). How many fifty-cent units?

A company had 114 employees initially. By morning, 58 more were hired. By midday, 24 were laid off. By afternoon, 38 left voluntarily. By evening, the final count multiplied by 6 and was measured in six-person teams (unit conversion). His partner company had 95 employees. How many team units were there?

An inventory had 150 items initially. In the morning, 27 were removed. By noon, 20 more were taken out. By afternoon, the remaining multiplied by 8. Then 608 items were lost. A distractor: another location had 95 items. When converted to 8-item cases (unit conversion), how many cases total?

A line had 90 items initially. By morning, 4 more arrived. It multiplied by 2 (doubling). Then by 7 (in groups of 7). At lunch, it was divided in half. By afternoon, it multiplied by 4. By evening, 1416 items were shipped. When measured in 2-item pairs (unit conversion), how many pairs?

A company had 236 units initially. In the morning, 61 were lost. By midday, 90 more were lost. The remaining tripled. By afternoon, 57 units arrived. By evening, the count quadrupled. A distractor: a related branch had 110 units. What was the final total?

A task list had 97 items in the morning. It multiplied by 6 (priority escalation). By afternoon, it was divided by 3 (consolidation). Then 36 items were added. By evening, 39 more were added. When the total was measured in hours (unit conversion), what was the count?

A project had 239 tasks in the morning. By mid-morning, 160 were completed. By noon, 21 more arrived. By afternoon, 51 more were assigned. By evening, 23 were removed. A distractor: another project had 115 tasks. How many final tasks were pending?

A project budget was 207 dollars. In the morning, 67 dollars were spent. The remaining multiplied by 7. By midday, 11 dollars were added. By afternoon, it multiplied by 8. By evening, 4477 dollars were removed. A distractor: another budget was 95 dollars. How much remained?

A team had 64 members. In the morning, 58 left. Then 3 more departed. The remaining sextupled (multiplied by 6). By afternoon, this was divided by 6 (undoing the multiplication). How many members did the team end with (compared to their partner team of 85)?

A project had 163 tasks initially. In the morning, 45 were added. By noon, 18 were removed. By afternoon, the remaining tripled. By late afternoon, it multiplied by 5. By evening, 29 more arrived. When converted to hours of work (unit change), how many tasks total?

An amount started at 34 dollars. In the morning, 56 were added. By midday, it multiplied by 7. By afternoon, 361 dollars were spent. By evening, the remaining multiplied by 9. Finally, 64 dollars were recovered. When measured in 9-dollar bundles (unit conversion), how much total?

A group had 161 members. In the morning, 123 left. By midday, 36 more departed. The remaining quadrupled by afternoon. By evening, it tripled. His associate managed 85 people. When converted to 3-person units (unit conversion), how many final units?

An investment started at 197 dollars. In the morning, 91 dollars were lost. By midday, the remaining multiplied by 5. By afternoon, it multiplied by 6 more. By evening, 2595 dollars were withdrawn. His friend had 110 dollars. When measured in tens (unit conversion), how many tens?

A task count was 28 initially. In the morning, it tripled. By midday, 74 tasks were added. By afternoon, 31 more were added. By evening, 66 more arrived. Finally, 61 were completed. His partner had 85 tasks. How many total tasks remained?

A total started at 226. In the morning, 18 were added. By noon, 65 more arrived. By afternoon, 78 more were added. The sum was divided equally into thirds. By evening, 18 were added. How many (measured as thirds or triple-units) were in the final count?

A base amount was 173 in the morning. By mid-morning, it multiplied by 5. By noon, it multiplied by 7. By afternoon, it multiplied by 7 again. By evening, it tripled. How many units was the final amount?

An amount was 147 dollars. In the morning, 24 were added. By noon, 99 dollars were spent. The remaining multiplied by 9. By afternoon, 534 dollars were withdrawn. By evening, the final amount divided in half. How many half-units (or half-dollars)?

An initial amount was 120. In the morning study session, 12 were added. By mid-morning, it tripled. By noon, 17 more were added. By afternoon, 13 more arrived. When measured in minutes (unit conversion), how many total?
